title: Father stops the quartet
summary: Foundation for music, parents not musical, father blocks a big program and quartet breaks up.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: you know. Did you enjoy singing in gospel? Oh yeah, yeah.
Was that kind of a primary foundation for what you would develop later, music?
Yeah, I think so. But we were, see we were all music and inclined, but I'm the only one that really did it professionally, you know, they all played around the house. I'll get to that too.
Were your father and mother, did they encourage you or did they play music?

No. I'mma tell you about that, see. But this thing with the quartet, one time, we were doing so good, you know, so people, they start paying us, giving us their money, you know. Like I said, we wouldn't ask for nothing but they volunteer, you know. And so one time they had a big thing, they had about ten, fifteen quartets. And we were the only kids, you know. All the rest was grown people, you know, grown men. And the people were there, looked like they all were there just to see us, you know. All the men, and I had a guard mother. She was blowing at this church, she was giving her that and she was really counting on it, you know. And my mother went and got all those suits. And my sister, coat suit to match us, match our suits. And my daddy had said it was all right for us to go, you know. So, and then, see my mother used to cut out of hair, boy's hair. So this is the first time we had been to the bar, but we were sharp, you know. We were all ready to go. Everybody, you know, all pumped up. So at the last minute we go, they go and my daddy tells us, well, you all can't go. And man, that's a big disappointment to everybody. Everybody, oh man. And so ever since then, that's where we just scrapped the quartet, man.
Your father just wouldn't let you all go out?

No, we just got disgusted, you know. And see, but what happened before that, when we would rehearse, he tried to get in that with us, you know. He wanted to practice with us like he wanted to join the quartet. But he was making a discord, you know. We'd tell him, say, man, you're making us all mad, you know. But he couldn't sing. No, he couldn't fit in with us, you know. And I guess he got pissed by that or something. I don't know what it was either. You see my mother was going.
Maybe he was a little jealous.

Yeah, I think so. And see, my mother, when we go on the convention, she'd go with us and I guess maybe he'd figure, well maybe, I'm not that she might get a man or something, you know. He's jealous I think, you know. Yeah, it seems.

Yeah. So after that the quartet broke up, you man, but no telling how far we could have went, you know. You know what I mean? You might have been bigger than Jackson 5, the son of people, you know. Do you remember what songs you all used to sing?
